chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Abu Abdillah, from Al-Hasan ibn Al-Husayn Al-Lu'lu'i, from Ibn Sinan, from Abu Al-Sahari Al-Nakhas, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him: 'A man drinks wine (khamr)?' He said: 'Bad is the drink, wine,' repeating this three times. Then he said: 'What do you mean?' I said: 'Does Allah accept his prayer?' He said: 'If Allah knows that when he rises from his prayer he seeks forgiveness and does not intend to return to it ever, Allah accepts his prayer from that moment; and if it is otherwise, that is up to Allah — when He wills He accepts it and when He wills He rejects it.'
ai.seo_question: Does drinking wine invalidate a Muslim's prayer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that the acceptance of a wine-drinker's prayer hinges on the sincerity of his repentance and his firm intention not to return to the sin. The Imam emphasizes that if Allah knows the individual will not revert, the prayer is accepted immediately; otherwise, its acceptance remains at Allah's discretion, highlighting the interplay between divine knowledge and human resolve in Shia jurisprudence.
